properties.name: camel.component.crypto.algorithm
properties.description: The standard name of the signature algorithm of the Java Cryptography Architecture, for example SHA256withRSA or SHA256withECDSA. It must match the type of the key, and the sign and verify endpoints must use the same algorithm.

properties.name: camel.component.crypto.alias
properties.description: The alias of the keystore entry: the sign operation signs with its private key, and the verify operation verifies with its certificate. If not set and the keystore holds exactly one entry, that entry is used.

properties.name: camel.component.crypto.autowired-enabled
properties.description: Whether autowiring is enabled. This is used for automatic autowiring options (the option must be marked as autowired) by looking up in the registry to find if there is a single instance of matching type, which then gets configured on the component. This can be used for automatic configuring JDBC data sources, JMS connection factories, AWS Clients, etc.

properties.name: camel.component.crypto.buffer-size
properties.description: The size in bytes of the buffer that reads the message body into the signature. It must be at least 1.

properties.name: camel.component.crypto.certificate
properties.description: The certificate whose public key the verify operation checks the signature with. A certificate found in the keystore under the alias is used instead, and this option is used instead of the publicKey option. The option is a java.security.cert.Certificate type.

properties.name: camel.component.crypto.certificate-name
properties.description: The name of a java.security.cert.Certificate bean in the registry to use as the certificate option. A name with no such bean is ignored.

properties.name: camel.component.crypto.clear-headers
properties.description: Whether to remove the headers whose names start with CamelSignature or CamelDigitalSignature after the operation succeeds. The sign operation removes them before it sets the signature header, and the verify operation also removes the signature header when its name matches.

properties.name: camel.component.crypto.configuration
properties.description: The configuration with the default options of all endpoints. Each endpoint gets a copy of it, and the options of the endpoint change only that copy. The option is a org.apache.camel.component.crypto.DigitalSignatureConfiguration type.

properties.name: camel.component.crypto.enabled
properties.description: Whether to enable auto configuration of the crypto component. This is enabled by default.

properties.name: camel.component.crypto.key-store-parameters
properties.description: The KeyStoreParameters (resource, type, password and provider of the keystore) that create the keystore of the keystore option. The keystore is loaded when this option is set. The option is a org.apache.camel.support.jsse.KeyStoreParameters type.

properties.name: camel.component.crypto.keystore
properties.description: The keystore that holds the private key for the sign operation and the certificate for the verify operation. The alias option selects the entry, or the only entry is used when the keystore holds exactly one. An entry found in the keystore is used instead of the privateKey, certificate and publicKey options. The option is a java.security.KeyStore type.

properties.name: camel.component.crypto.keystore-name
properties.description: The name of a java.security.KeyStore bean in the registry to use as the keystore option. A name with no such bean is ignored.

properties.name: camel.component.crypto.lazy-start-producer
properties.description: Whether the producer should be started lazy (on the first message). By starting lazy you can use this to allow CamelContext and routes to startup in situations where a producer may otherwise fail during starting and cause the route to fail being started. By deferring this startup to be lazy then the startup failure can be handled during routing messages via Camel's routing error handlers. Beware that when the first message is processed then creating and starting the producer may take a little time and prolong the total processing time of the processing.

properties.name: camel.component.crypto.password
properties.description: The password of the private key entry in the keystore, which the sign operation needs to read the key. It is not the password of the keystore itself.

properties.name: camel.component.crypto.private-key
properties.description: The private key that the sign operation signs with. A private key found in the keystore under the alias is used instead. The verify operation does not use it. The option is a java.security.PrivateKey type.

properties.name: camel.component.crypto.private-key-name
properties.description: The name of a java.security.PrivateKey bean in the registry to use as the privateKey option. A name with no such bean is ignored.

properties.name: camel.component.crypto.provider
properties.description: The name of the security provider that provides the signature algorithm, for example BC for Bouncy Castle. The provider must be installed. If not set, the first installed provider that supports the algorithm is used.

properties.name: camel.component.crypto.public-key
properties.description: The public key that the verify operation checks the signature with, when neither the keystore nor the certificate option gives a certificate. The sign operation does not use it. The option is a java.security.PublicKey type.

properties.name: camel.component.crypto.public-key-name
properties.description: The name of a java.security.PublicKey bean in the registry to use as the publicKey option. A name with no such bean is ignored.

properties.name: camel.component.crypto.secure-random
properties.description: The java.security.SecureRandom that the sign operation passes to Signature.initSign. If not set, the signature provider uses its own source of randomness. The option is a java.security.SecureRandom type.

properties.name: camel.component.crypto.secure-random-name
properties.description: The name of a java.security.SecureRandom bean in the registry to use as the secureRandom option. A name with no such bean is ignored.

properties.name: camel.component.crypto.signature-header-name
properties.description: The name of the header in which the sign operation stores the Base64 encoded signature, and from which the verify operation reads it. If not set, CamelDigitalSignature is used.

properties.name: camel.dataformat.crypto.algorithm
properties.description: The JCE algorithm name indicating the cryptographic algorithm that will be used.

properties.name: camel.dataformat.crypto.algorithm-parameter-spec
properties.description: A JCE AlgorithmParameterSpec used to initialize the Cipher. The option is a java.security.spec.AlgorithmParameterSpec type.

properties.name: camel.dataformat.crypto.buffer-size
properties.description: The size of the buffer used in the signature process.

properties.name: camel.dataformat.crypto.crypto-provider
properties.description: The name of the JCE Security Provider that should be used.

properties.name: camel.dataformat.crypto.enabled
properties.description: Whether to enable auto configuration of the crypto data format. This is enabled by default.

properties.name: camel.dataformat.crypto.init-vector
properties.description: Refers to a byte array containing the Initialization Vector that will be used to initialize the Cipher.

properties.name: camel.dataformat.crypto.inline
properties.description: Flag indicating that the configured IV should be inlined into the encrypted data stream. Is by default false.

properties.name: camel.dataformat.crypto.key
properties.description: Refers to the secret key to lookup from the register to use. The option is a java.security.Key type.

properties.name: camel.dataformat.crypto.mac-algorithm
properties.description: The JCE algorithm name indicating the Message Authentication algorithm.

properties.name: camel.dataformat.crypto.should-append-h-m-a-c
properties.description: Flag indicating that a Message Authentication Code should be calculated and appended to the encrypted data.
